I'm tagging as `bug` for now because a crash is never really intended, but I haven't checked whether this is an engine problem or an issue with the MRP specifically. It would be good to simplify the MRP to narrow down what's the real cause for the crash.

I may be missing something (just looked at it briefly), but this never returns nor breaks. How should it get out of the infinite loop?


We haven't solved the halting problem in GDScript yet :P so a crash is not unexpected (though we do have some measures in place to try to detect such issues before stack overflow but it's not bullet proof).

*Edit:* This doesn't seem to be the cause for the crash, this code is never reached, it crashes earlier. So again a more minimal MRP without unnecessary code would be good to narrow this down to the affected GDScript or core feature.

Here's the benchmark [script](https://github.com/blazium-engine/blazium/pull/399#issuecomment-2755881710) that causes the crash instead of the MRP, it runs fine unless you build with `dev_build=yes`.


```gdscript
extends Node2D

var root_node : Node
const TOTAL_NODES := 600
const MAX_CHILDREN_PER_NODE := 5
const NUM_ITERATIONS := 100
const SEARCH_PATTERNS : Array[String] = ["Child*", "Grandchild*", "GreatGrandchild*"]

func _ready() -> void:
	# Use this seed so every run uses same random numbers
	seed(42)

	# Create random tree, print names using find_children, and then delete tree
	root_node = Node.new()
	root_node.name = "Root"
	self.add_child(root_node)
	create_random_tree_with_random_names(root_node, 3, 4)
	print("Printing random tree to verify order is correct")
	print_tree_pretty_using_find_children(root_node)
	self.remove_child(root_node)
	root_node.queue_free()

	# Create new random tree to benchmark find_children
	root_node = Node.new()
	root_node.name = "Root"
	add_child(root_node)
	create_tree(root_node, 0)
	print("Benchmarking new tree with %d nodes" % [count_nodes(root_node)])
	
	# Start the continuous benchmark
	run_benchmark()

func print_tree_pretty_using_find_children(root: Node) -> void:
	print(root.name)
	
	# Get all children recursively
	var all_children = root.find_children("*", "", true, false)
	
	# Store depth information for each node
	var node_depth = {}
	for child in all_children:
		var depth = 0
		var current = child
		while current != root and current != null:
			depth += 1
			current = current.get_parent()
		node_depth[child] = depth
	
	# Print children with proper indentation
	for child in all_children:
		var depth = node_depth[child]
		if depth <= 0:  # Skip if it's the root
			continue
			
		# Build the prefix
		var prefix = ""
		if depth > 1:
			prefix += "│  ".repeat(depth - 1)
		prefix += "├─ "
		
		print(prefix + child.name)

func create_random_tree_with_random_names(parent : Node, max_depth := 3, max_children := 4, current_depth := 0) -> void:
	if current_depth >= max_depth: return

	var child_count := randi() % (max_children + 1)
	for i in range(child_count):
		var new_node := Node.new()
		new_node.name = "Node_" + str(randi() % 1000) + "_" + char(65 + randi() % 26)

		parent.add_child(new_node)

		create_random_tree_with_random_names(new_node, max_depth, max_children, current_depth + 1)

func create_tree(parent : Node, depth : int) -> void:
	if count_nodes(root_node) >= TOTAL_NODES:
		return
	
	var num_children = randi() % (MAX_CHILDREN_PER_NODE + 1)
	for i in range(num_children):
		var child = Node.new()
		if depth == 0:
			child.name = "Child%d" % i
		elif depth == 1:
			child.name = "Grandchild%d" % i
		else:
			child.name = "GreatGrandchild%d" % i
		parent.add_child(child)
		create_tree(child, depth + 1)

func count_nodes(node : Node) -> int:
	var count := 1  # Count the node itself
	for child in node.get_children():
		count += count_nodes(child)
	return count

func run_benchmark() -> void:
	while true:
		var start_time := Time.get_ticks_usec()
		var total_found := 0
		
		for i in range(NUM_ITERATIONS):
			# Randomly select a search pattern
			var pattern := SEARCH_PATTERNS[randi() % SEARCH_PATTERNS.size()]
			
			# Test find_children performance
			var children := root_node.find_children(pattern, "Node", true, false)
			total_found += children.size()
		
		var end_time := Time.get_ticks_usec()
		var total_time := (end_time - start_time) / 1000000.0  # Convert to seconds
		
		# Print results
		print("\nBenchmark Results:")
		print("Timestamp: %s" % Time.get_datetime_string_from_system())
		print("Total time: %.4f seconds" % total_time)
		print("Average time per iteration: %.4f milliseconds" % (total_time * 1000 / NUM_ITERATIONS))
		print("Average children found per iteration: %.2f" % (float(total_found) / NUM_ITERATIONS))
		
		# Wait for 2 seconds before the next run
		await get_tree().create_timer(2.0).timeout

func _exit_tree() -> void:
	# Clean up
	if is_instance_valid(root_node):
		root_node.queue_free()
```
building with `LTO` doesn't reproduce the issue.
It seems like some limits are different, causing the recursion to crash after exceeding a certain depth.

Master ([594d64e](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/594d64ec244b6b99321e2096987d4d69de4c8845) as of right now) built with `production=yes` using MSVC on Windows appears to have the same issue.

Please try lowering the [`MAX_CALL_DEPTH`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/594d64ec244b6b99321e2096987d4d69de4c8845/modules/gdscript/gdscript_function.h#L558) constant and the `debug/settings/gdscript/max_call_stack` project setting. Will this fix the crash? I've seen this or a similar crash where our infinite recursion protection failed because the stack overflow occurred before this limit was reached.

> Please try lowering the [`MAX_CALL_DEPTH`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/594d64ec244b6b99321e2096987d4d69de4c8845/modules/gdscript/gdscript_function.h#L558) constant and the `debug/settings/gdscript/max_call_stack` project setting. Will this fix the crash? I've seen this or a similar crash where our infinite recursion protection failed because the stack overflow occurred before this limit was reached.

lowered both of them to 512 and it still crashes in dev_build, Following the stack trace, method `count_nodes` is called with p_args that has a very large int number.

when Using LTO, lowering `max_stack_trace` to 512 stops the game with stack overflow. but it doesn't happen in dev_build, the crash happens before reaching the `max_stack_trace`.

I think it's probably just fat stack frames because the optimisations are off.
Here's the -fstack-usage output for the four functions in the recursive part of the trace.

For a regular build:

| function | stack frame | qualifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDScriptFunction::call | 720 | dynamic |
| GDScriptInstance::callp | 128 | dynamic,bounded |
| Object::callp | 176 | dynamic,bounded |
| Variant::callp | 112 | static |

For a dev build:

| function | stack frame | qualifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GDScriptFunction::call | 16976 | dynamic |
| GDScriptInstance::callp | 96 | dynamic,bounded |
| Object::callp | 240 | dynamic,bounded |
| Variant::callp | 192 | static |

Qualifier `dynamic` means it's not really a reliable number. So it might not actually be 17KB a call, but we would only need 8KB to blow the default 8MB stack on Linux, before we hit our GDScript call stack limit of 1024.
